article.title: 1Password’s new browser integration for Claude changes how AI uses your credentials
article.summary: As AI agents tackle more tasks, such as managing online accounts , authentication has become a practical engineering problem. For example, companies like Coinbase are already running over a thousand agents in production . Enter a new 1Password feature for Claude that is designed to let a fleet of agents sign in without ever exposing passwords to the LLM.  The company calls this new browser integration a “zero-exposure security framework.” Credentials are decrypted only when needed and passed directly to the browser, allowing Claude to complete an action without ever seeing the underlying password or one-time authentication code. article.title_zh: 1Password 推出 Claude 新型瀏覽器集成功能——改變 AI 使用認證方式
article.summary_zh: 隨著 AI 代理承擔越來越多任務（如管理在線帳戶），身份驗證已成為實際的工程問題，新推出的 1Password for Claude 功能旨在讓 AI 代理隊伍能夠安全地進行大規模生產操作。

article.title: The agent security gap: 54% of enterprises have already had an AI agent incident, and most still let agents share credentials
article.summary: Across 107 enterprises, AI agents are being given real access to systems and data while the controls meant to contain them lag behind. More than half have already had a confirmed agent security incident or a near-miss; only about a third give every agent its own scoped identity, and most agents still share credentials; and only three in ten isolate their highest-risk agents. The security stack is overwhelmingly borrowed from the model providers and hyperscalers rather than purpose-built for agents, spending remains a thin slice of the security budget, and enterprises are evenly split on whether their defenses are keeping pace with AI-enabled attackers. article.title_zh: AI 代理安全差距：54% 企業已經遭遇 AI 代理事件，大多數仍讓代理共享憑證
article.summary_zh: 在 107 家企業中，AI 代理被授予系統和資料的實際存取權，而控制它們的措施卻滯後。超過一半已經遭遇已確認的代理安全事件或近乎失誤；只有約三分之一的企業為每個代理配置自己的作用域身份，大多數代理仍然共享憑證。

article.title: Platform engineering’s new job: serving environments at agent speed
article.summary: Platform engineering has won the argument. Some 90% of organizations have adopted at least one internal platform ; golden paths are orthodoxy, and environment requests that once took days now close in hours. By the standard the discipline set for itself, that is victory. Then the most demanding customer the platform has ever had showed up, and it is not a developer. A coding agent that wants to validate its work requests an environment the way a client calls an API: in bursts, concurrently, with a lifetime measured in minutes and an expectation measured in seconds. A 100-developer organization in which each engineer supervises a few agent sessions per day generates hundreds of environment requests before lunch.
